messages:
omar (new): Hi! First day — hitting a weird one on Ubuntu. `docker compose up` fails because postgres container immediately exits with "address already in use". I didn't even get the init error. Anyone know what process usually holds 5432 on dev boxes?

omar (new): `docker compose logs postgres` shows: 
```
package_postgres_1 | FATAL:  could not bind IPv4 socket: Address already in use
package_postgres_1 | DETAIL:  Is another postmaster already running on port 5432?
```

jean (eng): welcome Omar! :wave: Common cause: a system postgres (apt/apt-get installed) running as a service, or another DB like Timescale, or leftover docker container. Try `ss -ltnp | grep 5432` or `sudo systemctl status postgresql` to check.

mike (infra): +1. If you have `postgresql` installed from distro, `sudo systemctl stop postgresql` will free the port. If you want containers to own the port but keep system postgres, map the compose port to a different host port, e.g. "55432:5432" and set `DATABASE_URL=postgres://user:pass@localhost:55432/db` in `.env.local`.

omar (new): I ran `sudo systemctl stop postgresql` and `docker compose up` starts the container fine. Is it safe to keep system postgres stopped? Will it come back after reboot?

jean (eng): it will restart on reboot unless you disable it. `sudo systemctl disable --now postgresql` will stop+prevent auto-start. But if you prefer not to change system services, remapping the host port is low-friction. For reproducible dev environments we usually use the container port mapped to 5432 so other team members can assume `localhost:5432` — but if you already have a local Postgres for other projects, remap locally.

mike (infra): quick checklist: 
1) `ss -ltnp | grep 5432` to find PID
2) `sudo systemctl stop postgresql` or `sudo kill <pid>` if it's another process
3) consider `docker compose down --remove-orphans` in case an old container holds the port
4) prefer named volumes for DB data (`dev_pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data`) to avoid bind-mount ownership issues

omar (new): great — stopped systemd postgres and container came up. One last thing: our `scripts/db-reset` uses host `psql` and fails for me when I remap to 55432 because it still tries default port. Should I update my `.env.local`?

jean (eng): yes update `.env.local` with the right DATABASE_URL or set `PGPORT=55432` for local scripts. Alternatively run the CLI inside the container: `docker compose exec postgres psql -U redwood -d redwood_dev -c "SELECT 1"` so scripts don't rely on host port mapping. We try to avoid touching DB files on host.

mike (infra): addendum: if you ever want to run both system and container DB simultaneously, set different ports for one of them. For onboarding notes we should add a troubleshooting line about "port 5432 in use => check system postgres". I'll add it to the docs.

omar (new): thanks everyone — resolved. I'll add the `.env.local` change to my personal checklist and disable system postgres on my laptop for dev. Appreciate the fast help! :tada:
